Predict trait values for species

Source: R/predict.R
predict.phylogp_fit.Rd

Posterior predictive distributions of the trait for species in the tree: species that were fitted (smoothed values) or species in the tree without trait data (phylogenetic imputation, i.e. kriging on the tree). Each prediction conditions on all observed species, through the kernel and the regression part of the model, and integrates over the posterior draws.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'phylogp_fit'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  tree = NULL,
  type = c("response", "latent"),
  ndraws = 500,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95),
  seed = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A phylogp_fit.

newdata

Optional data frame with the predictor values of the species to predict, named as in the fit (row names or the species column). Its species must be in tree. If NULL, the fitted species are predicted.

tree

Tree containing the species to predict; by default the tree given to phylo_gp().

type

"response" (a new observation of the trait, including residual variation from k_white() and, for fits with several rows per species, the within-species variation) or "latent" (the evolutionary process at the tip).

ndraws

Number of posterior draws used.

probs

Quantiles to report.

seed

Random seed for draw selection and quantiles.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame with one row per species: whether it was observed, posterior mean, standard deviation and quantiles.

Details

For kernels with latent values, the values a new species needs are drawn for each posterior draw from their conditional prior given the fitted ones: relaxed log rates and latent slope deviations by a Brownian bridge along the fitted branch the species joins and Brownian motion along its own branch, a Student-t variance multiplier from its inverse-gamma prior; rates through time keep the time bins of the fitted tree.

References

Garland T. Jr., Ives A.R. 2000. Using the past to predict the present: Confidence intervals for regression equations in phylogenetic comparative methods. The American Naturalist. 155:346–364.

Rasmussen C.E., Williams C.K.I. 2006. Gaussian processes for machine learning. Cambridge, MA: MIT Press.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- phylo_gp(y ~ x, d, tree, k_bm() + k_white())
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = 1.2, row.names = "missing_species"))
} # }
